{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "The question asks for a paying customer within 90 days. Idea B's own sourced evidence, from dashp's founder via Starter Story, says each closed deal takes about 5 months of in-person trust-building. That alone puts B's typical first sale outside the window.",
    "Idea A has a sourced, near-zero-cost self-serve channel: GitHub Marketplace listing with built-in pricing plans. A solo operator running AI agents can use this without in-person selling. B's channels are office visits (about 5 months per deal) or a PestWorld booth costing $3,475 to $4,500, and 2026 booths are already sold out.",
    "Idea A shows small-team price points sold self-serve, not only enterprise contracts. Testhide Cloud starts at $49/mo and Harness AI add-ons run $20 to $50 per developer per month. This suggests a cheap wedge buyer exists below Develocity's contact-sales tier.",
    "B's ICP is described by its own seed source as only 'hundreds' of companies and unsuited to performance marketing. That shrinks the pool of fast first buyers. A's target, any team with slow or flaky CI, is broader, and its pain is documented across many CI jobs and companies.",
    "A's main risks are trust and false negatives when a tool gates merges, plus the cold start with no history. These can be partly sidestepped by launching as an advisory-only flake flagger. B's main risk is the length of its trust-based sales cycle, and AI agents do not obviously shorten it.",
    "B does have stronger proof that someone pays: dashp at about $100k ARR, and D2DHQ's published $149 to $499/mo pricing. But that proof sits next to a sales motion that conflicts with the 90-day constraint."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B's demand evidence comes from the wrong party. One item is an anonymous usacomplaints.com post by a pest control tech about commission shortfalls at a single company. The other is a single litigated commission dispute. Both reflect reps' grievances about unpaid wages, not owners or sales-ops managers (the stated payer) wanting to buy tracking software. Neither shows willingness to pay for a tool.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate-to-low confidence. A's own demand evidence is also weak. Its key quote and statistic come from Trunk, a flaky-test vendor's content piece. None of the OSS clones are shown to be monetized. Its six-week MVP timeline is unsourced. B has the more concrete proof that customers pay, and loses mainly because sourced evidence puts its sales cycle at about 5 months, longer than the 90-day window."
}
